title: Anti-concentration for $B$-reasonable variables
statement: Let $X$ be measurable on a probability space, assume $X\in L^4$, $X^2$ and $X^4$ are integrable, and $\E X^2>0$. If $B\ge1$ and $\E X^4\le B(\E X^2)^2$, then for every $0\le t\le1$, $\Pr[X^2>t^2\E X^2]\ge(1-t^2)^2/B$.
hypotheses_covered: X is B-reasonable (fourth moment controlled by squared second moment)
second moment E[X^2] is finite (X^2 integrable)
fourth moment E[X^4] is finite (X^4 integrable)
replaced:
If $X$ is $B$-reasonable and not equivalent to $0$, then for every $t \in [0,1]$,
\[
\Pr\bigl[\,|X| > t\,\norm{X}_2\,\bigr] \ge \frac{(1-t^2)^2}{B}.
\]
